title: Monarchy of Rana Regime Nepal: Brief Discussion राणाकालीन नेपालको राजतन्त्रः संक्षिप्त चर्चा
nepali: नागवंशद्वारा राजतन्त्रात्मक मुलुकका रूपमा सङ्गठित प्रयास थालिएको नेपालमा विभिन्न राजवंशले शासन गरेको पाइन्छ । सुरुदेखि नै शक्तिशाली राजतन्त्र कायम रहेको हुँदा शासन व्यवस्थामा राजाको स्थान सर्वोच्च हुने परम्परामै हुर्किएको नेपाली समाजले राजालाई भगवानकै अवतारका रूपमा हेर्ने–मान्ने गर्दथ्यो । शक्तिका आधारमा स्थापना, विकास र विस्तार हुने परम्पराझैं गरेर विभिन्न राज्यहरूको निर्माण, विखण्डन र विनास भएका घटनाहरूले गर्दा ५४ वटा राज्यहरूमा विभक्त नेपाली भूभागलाई गोरखाका राजा पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले एकीकृत नेपाल निर्माणको बाटोमा बढाएर आधुनिक नेपालको शिलान्यास गरेका थिए । विपन्न र आफन्तहरूद्वारा अपहेलित गोरखा राज्यलाई आत्मनिर्भर–सम्पन्न राष्ट्र बनाउने सपना देखेका राजा पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले राजा र जनता बिच मेल कायम गरेर देशलाई सम्पूर्ण देशवाशीहरूको साझा सम्पत्ति हो भन्ने भावना जनताको हृदयमा जगाउन सकेकाले नै आफ्नो राज्य विस्तार अभियानलाई नेपाल एकीकरण अभियानमा बदल्न सकेका हुन् । राष्ट्रिय उन्नती, विकास र सुदृढताका लागि राजशक्ति र जनशक्तिको मेल आवश्यक छ भन्ने मान्यताका आधारमा गतिशील भएर अपार जनसमर्थन पाएकाले एकीकरणकर्ताको स्थान पाएका पृथ्वीनारायण शाहका उत्तराधिकारीहरूले उनको नीतिलाई कायम राख्न सकेनन् । राजा भनेको जनताको रषक एवं हितको संरक्षण गर्ने संस्था प्रमुख हो भन्ने यथार्थ विपरीत उत्रिएका उनीहरूले सत्ता सङ्घर्षको खेलमा लागेर राज्यका महत्त्वपूर्ण भारदारहरूलाई बेवास्ता गरेर चाटुकार–रंगरेलियाका नायकहरूलाई विश्वास गर्ने र पुराना भारदारहरूलाई मृत्युदण्डको सजाय दिनेसम्मका कार्यहरू गरेपछि राजा प्रजाको एकता–विश्वास खण्डित हुन गयो । राज परिवार नै सत्ता खेल–गुटबन्दी र षड्यन्त्रमा लागेपछि बढेको भारदारी षडयन्त्रले राणा शासनको उदय गराएर राजालाई खोपाको देउताको रूपमा पुर्‌याइदियो ।
american_english: In Nepal, where organized efforts toward a monarchical country were initiated by the Naga dynasty, various royal dynasties are found to have ruled. Because a powerful monarchy was maintained from the beginning, Nepali society, raised in the tradition where the king's position was supreme in the system of governance, regarded and revered the king as an incarnation of God himself. In keeping with the tradition of establishment, development, and expansion on the basis of power, through events involving the creation, fragmentation, and destruction of various states, King Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha advanced the Nepali territory divided into 54 states along the path of building a unified Nepal, laying the foundation of modern Nepal. Having dreamed of making the impoverished Gorkha state, slighted by relatives, into a self-reliant and prosperous nation, King Prithvi Narayan Shah was able to transform his state expansion campaign into the Nepal unification campaign precisely because he maintained harmony between king and people and awakened in the hearts of the people the feeling that the country was the shared property of all citizens. Moving on the basis of the belief that the union of royal power and people's power is necessary for national progress, development, and consolidation, and having earned the status of unifier through immense popular support, Prithvi Narayan Shah's successors could not sustain his policy. Turning against the reality that the king is the head of the institution that protects the people and guards their interests, they engaged in the game of power struggle, ignored the important court nobles of the state, trusted flatterers and revelers, and went so far as to sentence veteran nobles to death, after which the unity and trust between king and subjects became fractured. Once the royal family itself became involved in power games, factionalism, and conspiracy, the escalating court intrigues brought about the rise of Rana rule and reduced the king to a deity in a niche.

Once the royal household itself became embroiled in power struggles, factionalism and intrigue, the escalating court conspiracies brought about the rise of Rana rule and reduced the monarch to a deity in a niche.

translator_notes: Source text traces the shift from Prithvi Narayan Shah's unifying statecraft to factional court intrigue and the rise of the Rana oligarchy. The typo 'रषक' in the source is translated according to its intended meaning 'रक्षक' (protector). The cultural idiom 'खोपाको देउता' (a deity kept in an alcove/niche, powerless figurehead) is rendered idiomatically. Strict sentence order preserved across all 7 sentences.
